ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A charged sphere with mass $m$ and charge $+q$ is attached to one end of an inextensible insulating thread. The other end of the thread is fixed at point O. The length of the thread is $L$. A uniform electric field is applied horizontally, and the sphere is at rest at point A, forming an angle of $\theta = 30^\circ$ with the vertical direction. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$ ($\sin37^\circ = 0.6$, $\cos37^\circ = 0.8$).

1. The magnitude and direction of the field strength.
2. If the sphere is pulled to point B, which is at the same height as point O, and released from rest, calculate the speed of the sphere when it passes through the lowest point C and the tension in the string at this point.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$\frac{\sqrt{3}mg}{3q}$, horizontally to the right
$\sqrt{2gL(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})}$, $3mg - \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}mg$, direction along the rope vertically upward

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the fixed point O is at the upper left, B is directly to the right of O and at the same height as O; C is directly below O; the small ball is located at point A, at the lower right of O, and the angle between rope OA and the vertical direction is labeled θ. The dashed arc indicates that the small ball can move along an arc with O as the center and length L as the radius from B through A to C. The small ball is labeled as having mass m and charge +q. Reasoning: When at rest and in equilibrium at point A, the small ball is subject to gravity mg downward, electric field force qE horizontally, and rope tension T along AO pointing toward O. Since the tension has a leftward horizontal component, to balance this component, the electric field force on the positive charge must be to the right, so the electric field direction is horizontally to the right. Vertical equilibrium: T cosθ = mg; horizontal equilibrium: qE = T sinθ. Dividing the two equations gives qE = mg tanθ, so E = (mg/q)tan30° = √3mg/(3q). Released from rest at point B to the lowest point C, the rope tension does no work throughout. From B to C, the vertical height decreases by L, so gravity does work mgL; the electric field force is to the right, while the horizontal displacement of the small ball from B to C is to the left, with magnitude L, so the electric field force does work -qEL. Therefore, by the kinetic energy theorem: 1/2 mv^2 = mgL - qEL = mgL - q(√3mg/(3q))L = mgL(1 - √3/3). Therefore v = √[2gL(1 - √3/3)]. At the lowest point C, the rope is vertical, the electric field force is horizontal, and there is no radial component along the rope direction. Writing the equation radially upward: T - mg = mv^2/L. Substituting v^2 = 2gL(1 - √3/3), obtain T = mg + 2mg(1 - √3/3) = 3mg - 2√3mg/3, with direction vertically upward along the rope.

method.method_draft: Use direct Cartesian force balance at A, then work-energy from B to C. First read the diagram: O is the fixed point at the upper left, A lies down and to the right of O with the string making angle θ to the vertical, B is horizontally to the right of O, and C is directly below O. From the text, θ=30°, mass m, charge +q, string length L, and the field is horizontal. At equilibrium at A, resolve tension along the string: vertical balance gives T cosθ=mg and horizontal balance requires qE=T sinθ, so E=(mg/q)tan30°=sqrt(3)mg/(3q), directed to the right because the positive charge must be pulled rightward to balance the leftward horizontal component of tension. For the release from B, use work-energy because tension does no work. From B to C, gravity does +mgL work and the electric force does -qEL work since displacement is leftward while the electric force is rightward. Thus (1/2)mv^2=mgL-qEL, giving v=sqrt(2gL(1-sqrt(3)/3)). At C the string is vertical, so the electric force is horizontal and has no radial component; radial dynamics gives T-mg=mv^2/L, hence T=3mg-2sqrt(3)mg/3 upward along the rope.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中固定点 O 在左上方，B 在 O 的正右方且与 O 等高；C 在 O 的正下方；小球位于 A 点，在 O 的右下方，绳 OA 与竖直方向夹角标为 θ。虚线弧线表示小球可沿以 O 为圆心、长度 L 为半径的圆弧从 B 经 A 到 C 运动。小球标注为质量 m、带电量 +q。

推理：在 A 点静止平衡时，小球受重力 mg 向下、电场力 qE 水平、绳张力 T 沿 AO 指向 O。由于张力有向左的水平分量，为平衡该分量，正电荷所受电场力必须向右，因此电场方向水平向右。竖直方向平衡：T cosθ = mg；水平方向平衡：qE = T sinθ。两式相除得 qE = mg tanθ，所以 E = (mg/q)tan30° = √3mg/(3q)。

从 B 点由静止释放到最低点 C，绳张力始终不做功。B 到 C 的竖直高度下降 L，所以重力做功 mgL；电场力向右，而小球从 B 到 C 的水平位移向左，大小为 L，所以电场力做功 -qEL。因此由动能定理：1/2 mv^2 = mgL - qEL = mgL - q(√3mg/(3q))L = mgL(1 - √3/3)。所以 v = √[2gL(1 - √3/3)]。

在最低点 C，绳竖直，电场力水平，没有沿绳方向的径向分量。径向向上列方程：T - mg = mv^2/L。代入 v^2 = 2gL(1 - √3/3)，得 T = mg + 2mg(1 - √3/3) = 3mg - 2√3mg/3，方向沿绳竖直向上。

2. 小球经过最低点 C 时速度为 v = √[2gL(1 - √3/3)]；此时绳的张力为 T = 3mg - 2√3mg/3，方向沿绳竖直向上。

method.method_draft: Use the combined constant-force/effective-potential viewpoint. From the image, identify that the bob at A is displaced down-right from O, while B is at the right end of the horizontal radius and C is the bottom point of the circle. From the text, the bob is at rest at A at θ=30° in a horizontal electric field. In equilibrium, the string must align opposite the resultant of the two constant forces: gravity mg downward and electric force qE horizontally. Since the resultant points down-right along OA, tanθ=qE/mg, so E=sqrt(3)mg/(3q), to the right. For the motion, combine gravity and electric force into one conservative constant force F=(qE right)+(mg down). The kinetic energy gained from B to C equals the dot product of this resultant force with the displacement from B to C: displacement is one radius left and one radius down, so W=mgL-qEL. This immediately gives v=sqrt(2gL(1-sqrt(3)/3)). At C, project the same resultant force along the radial direction toward O; only gravity contributes radially opposite the inward direction and the electric force is perpendicular to the string. Therefore T-mg=mv^2/L and T=3mg-2sqrt(3)mg/3 upward.

method.method_draft: Use angular torque and angular-energy integration. From the diagram, take the angle φ from the downward vertical through O, with A at φ=30°, B at φ=90°, and C at φ=0°. The text gives that A is a rest equilibrium and the electric field is horizontal. About O, the torque from gravity is -mgL sinφ and the torque from a rightward electric force on +q is +qEL cosφ. Static equilibrium at φ=30° requires qEL cos30°=mgL sin30°, so E=(mg/q)tan30°=sqrt(3)mg/(3q), directed rightward. For the release from B, use the rotational work-energy relation dK=τ dφ. Integrate τ=qEL cosφ-mgL sinφ from φ=90° to φ=0°: ΔK=∫(qEL cosφ-mgL sinφ)dφ=mgL-qEL. Hence v=sqrt(2gL(1-sqrt(3)/3)). At C, apply the normal/radial equation with inward direction upward: the torque method has already supplied v, and the radial forces are T upward and mg downward, while qE is tangential, so T-mg=mv^2/L and T=3mg-2sqrt(3)mg/3 upward along the string.

raw_record.original_question:
A charged sphere with mass $m$ and charge $+q$ is attached to one end of an inextensible insulating thread. The other end of the thread is fixed at point O. The length of the thread is $L$. A uniform electric field is applied horizontally, and the sphere is at rest at point A, forming an angle of $\theta = 30^\circ$ with the vertical direction. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$ ($\sin37^\circ = 0.6$, $\cos37^\circ = 0.8$).

1. Find the magnitude and direction of the electric field strength.
2. If the sphere is pulled to point B, which is at the same height as point O, and released from rest, calculate the speed of the sphere when it passes through the lowest point C and the tension in the string at this point.
raw_record.answer:
$\frac{\sqrt{3}mg}{3q}$, horizontally to the right
$\sqrt{2gL\left(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)}$, $3mg-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}mg$, direction along the rope vertically upward
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the fixed point O is at the upper left, B is directly to the right of O and at the same height as O; C is directly below O; the small ball is located at point A, at the lower right of O, and the angle between rope OA and the vertical direction is labeled θ. The dashed arc indicates that the small ball can move along an arc with O as the center and length L as the radius from B through A to C. The small ball is labeled as having mass m and charge +q.

Reasoning: When at rest and in equilibrium at point A, the small ball is subject to gravity mg downward, electric field force qE horizontally, and rope tension T along AO pointing toward O. Since the tension has a leftward horizontal component, to balance this component, the electric field force on the positive charge must be to the right, so the electric field direction is horizontally to the right. Vertical equilibrium: T cosθ = mg; horizontal equilibrium: qE = T sinθ. Dividing the two equations gives qE = mg tanθ, so E = (mg/q)tan30° = √3mg/(3q).

Released from rest at point B to the lowest point C, the rope tension does no work throughout. From B to C, the vertical height decreases by L, so gravity does work mgL; the electric field force is to the right, while the horizontal displacement of the small ball from B to C is to the left, with magnitude L, so the electric field force does work -qEL. Therefore, by the kinetic energy theorem: 1/2 mv^2 = mgL - qEL = mgL - q(√3mg/(3q))L = mgL(1 - √3/3). Therefore v = √[2gL(1 - √3/3)].

At the lowest point C, the rope is vertical, the electric field force is horizontal, and there is no radial component along the rope direction. Writing the equation radially upward: T - mg = mv^2/L. Substituting v^2 = 2gL(1 - √3/3), obtain T = mg + 2mg(1 - √3/3) = 3mg - 2√3mg/3, with direction vertically upward along the rope.

Reasoning: When at rest and in equilibrium at point A, the small ball is subject to gravity mg downward, electric field force qE horizontally, and rope tension T along AO pointing toward O. Since the tension has a leftward horizontal component, to balance this component, the electric field force on the positive charge must be to the right, so the electric field direction is horizontally to the right. Vertical equilibrium: T cosθ = mg; horizontal equilibrium: qE = T sinθ. Dividing the two equations gives qE = mg tanθ, so E = (mg/q)tan30° = √3mg/(3q).

Released from rest at point B to the lowest point C, the rope tension does no work throughout. From B to C, the vertical height decreases by L, so gravity does work mgL; the electric field force is to the right, while the horizontal displacement of the small ball from B to C is to the left, with magnitude L, so the electric field force does work -qEL. Therefore, by the kinetic energy theorem: 1/2 mv^2 = mgL - qEL = mgL - q(√3mg/(3q))L = mgL(1 - √3/3). Therefore v = √[2gL(1 - √3/3)].

At the lowest point C, the rope is vertical, the electric field force is horizontal, and there is no radial component along the rope direction. Writing the equation radially upward: T - mg = mv^2/L. Substituting v^2 = 2gL(1 - √3/3), obtain T = mg + 2mg(1 - √3/3) = 3mg - 2√3mg/3, with direction vertically upward along the rope.
